content.p: A taxi from Rye to Melbourne Airport is a door-to-door transfer from the southern end of the Mornington Peninsula, across the city to Tullamarine, with no train changes and no long-term parking to pay for. Taxi Peninsula runs this trip 24 hours a day in sedans and wheelchair accessible vehicles, and the trip facts below show the usual distance, drive time and a fare estimate based on our own rates.

content.h2: How long does the trip from Rye to the airport take?

content.p: The drive time in the box above is a typical figure, but Rye sits about as far from Tullamarine as you can get while still being in greater Melbourne, so the real time depends heavily on when you travel. The usual route leaves Rye along Point Nepean Road or the Mornington Peninsula Freeway, heads north on Peninsula Link and then crosses the south-eastern suburbs and the city on the freeway network. A dawn departure on a weekday is quick until the inner suburbs wake up. A mid-afternoon run on a Friday before school holidays can be much slower.

For domestic flights, aim to be dropped off with enough time to check bags and clear security without rushing. For international flights, allow more. If you are unsure, ask us when you book and we will suggest a pick-up time that leaves a sensible buffer.

content.h2: How much is a taxi from Rye to Melbourne Airport?

content.p: See the estimate above. It is worked out from our standard rates, but the final fare depends on traffic, the time of day and any tolls on the route the driver takes. Late-night and early-morning travel can also make a difference. If you would rather know the amount before you leave, ask for a fixed quote when you book and we will confirm it by SMS or email.

content.h2: When should I book my airport taxi from Rye?

content.p: As early as you know your flight details. Bookings are recommended for every trip, and for airport runs from the southern Peninsula they matter more because the distance is long and early-morning slots fill first. Booking online takes about two minutes, or you can phone 0468 323 211.

ul: Book at least the day before for any flight that leaves before breakfast.
Tell us your airline so we head to the right terminal; international flights use Terminal 2.
Add your flight number if you are booking the return trip, so we can track it.
Mention surfboards, golf bags, prams or car seats in the booking notes.

content.h2: Can you fit our luggage and a wheelchair?

content.p: A sedan suits most couples and solo travellers with a couple of suitcases. If you are heading away as a family with several bags, a pram or sports gear, the Maxi WAT gives you far more room. It was built for wheelchair users, with a hydraulic hoist and space for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, so it also handles a big holiday load easily.

If you travel in your wheelchair, choose the wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or the Maxi WAT for heavier power chairs. Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning, and carers travel with you. Our drivers help with bags from your front door to the departures kerb.

content.h2: How do I get back to Rye after my flight lands?

content.p: Book the return trip when you book the outbound one and add your flight number. We track the flight, so if you land early or the plane is held up, the driver adjusts rather than leaving you waiting or racing to catch up. Pick-up areas at the airport are separate from the terminal doors and can change, so we confirm the meeting point by SMS or phone once you land.

After a long-haul flight, the trip back down to Rye is a good time to close your eyes. We take you to your door, help with the bags, and you are home without a bus connection or a hunt for your car in a parking lot.

faq.q: Is a taxi from Rye to the airport worth it compared with parking?
faq.a: It depends on how long you are away and how many people are travelling. Long-term airport parking adds up over a week or more, and you still have to drive across Melbourne at both ends. Check the estimate on this page, compare it with your parking costs, and ask for a fixed quote if you want a set amount before deciding.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from Sorrento or Blairgowrie instead of Rye?
faq.a: Yes. We collect from anywhere on the southern Peninsula, including Sorrento, Blairgowrie, Tootgarook and Rosebud, as well as holiday houses and caravan parks. Give us the full address and any gate code or unit number in the booking notes, and the driver will come to your door rather than meeting you on the main road.

faq.q: Do you accept MPTP cards on airport trips?
faq.a: Yes, we accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards for eligible passengers, as well as NDIS and aged-care accounts. Let us know which one you are using when you book so the driver is ready. A carer can travel with you, and our wheelchair accessible vehicles take you to the airport in your own chair.

The trip facts box below gives the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from our own rates.

content.h2: What is the usual route from Sorrento to Tullamarine?

content.p: Most trips leave Sorrento along Point Nepean Road through Blairgowrie and Rye before joining the Mornington Peninsula Freeway. From there the driver heads north on Peninsula Link towards the south-eastern freeways and then crosses Melbourne to the airport. Toll roads such as EastLink or CityLink may be used depending on traffic, and the driver picks the route that makes sense on the day.

It is one of the longer airport transfers we do. In summer, Point Nepean Road through the southern towns can crawl with holiday traffic, so early pick-ups during January and long weekends are a good idea even if your flight is not until midday.

Coming from the hotels and guesthouses along the Sorrento foreshore, or from a holiday house tucked up a sandy track in Blairgowrie, the driver will come right to you. Add any directions to the booking notes, such as a shared driveway, a gate code or the easiest place to stop, and you will not need to drag your suitcases down to the main road. Early-morning pick-ups in the back streets are often in the dark, so leaving a porch light on helps too.

content.h2: How much does the taxi cost?

content.p: See the estimate above. That figure comes from our standard rates, and the fare on the day depends on traffic, the time of day and tolls. If you prefer certainty for a long trip like this, ask for a fixed quote when you book. We will confirm the price along with your booking by SMS or email.

content.h2: How far ahead should I book from Sorrento?

content.p: Book once your flight is confirmed. Sorrento is at the far end of our service area, and drivers need to be planned in for early starts, so the night before is the latest we would suggest for dawn departures. During school holidays and the summer peak, booking several days ahead gives you more choice of vehicle.

ul: Use the online booking form, which takes about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.
Add your hotel name and room or the holiday house address, plus any access notes.
Tell us if you are flying domestic or international and with which airline.
Book your return transfer at the same time and include the flight number.

content.h2: What if we have lots of bags or someone uses a wheelchair?

content.p: Sorrento holidays often end with a car-load of beach gear, so tell us what you are bringing. A sedan is fine for a couple with suitcases. A family with a pram, booster seats and boogie boards will be more comfortable in the Maxi WAT, which has room for six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs and loads through a hydraulic hoist.

For a passenger who stays in their wheelchair, the accessible van with its rear ramp takes one wheelchair plus four others, and the Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs or a heavier power chair. Four-point wheelchair restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning come as standard. Our drivers help from the front door to the terminal kerb.

content.h2: Can you collect us from the airport and bring us back to Sorrento?

content.p: Yes. Add your flight number to the booking and we track the arrival, adjusting for delays or an early landing. Because the airport’s pick-up zones are not right outside the terminal doors and can change, we send the meeting point by SMS or confirm it by phone. Then it is a straight run back down the Peninsula to your door.

Visitors who have been staying in Sorrento and are flying out at the end of their holiday can book the trip the same way. Tell us the checkout time and your flight, and we will suggest a pick-up that gives you a relaxed last morning without a dash up the freeway.

faq.q: Can you pick up from a Sorrento hotel at four in the morning?
faq.a: Yes. We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so pre-dawn hotel pick-ups are routine. Book ahead, tell us the hotel name and whether you will be waiting in the lobby or at the front entrance, and the driver will be there at the agreed time. We confirm your booking by SMS or email.

faq.q: Is there a train from Sorrento to the airport?
faq.a: No. The southern Peninsula has no train line, so travelling by public transport means a bus to a station, a train into the city and then a separate airport connection. With luggage, that is several changes. A taxi takes you directly from your door in Sorrento to the terminal with your bags in one vehicle.

faq.q: Can I get a fixed price for Sorrento to Melbourne Airport?
faq.a: Yes, fixed quotes are available on request. Tell us your pick-up address, the terminal, the time and the vehicle you need when booking, and we will confirm a set price. Otherwise the fare is metered, and the estimate shown on this page and in the booking form gives you a realistic idea in advance.

faq.q: Will the driver wait if my flight is delayed?

Some Peninsula travellers choose Avalon because a particular flight time or fare suits them better, or because they are heading somewhere served from there. That is a perfectly good reason to fly from Avalon, but the road trip is a real part of the journey. Treat it as you would any long drive, with a realistic departure time rather than a hopeful one.

content.h2: How much does a taxi to Avalon cost?

content.p: See the estimate above. Starting from further south, such as Rosebud or Sorrento, adds to it, and starting from Frankston takes some off. content.h2: How early should I leave for an Avalon flight?

content.p: Leave earlier than you think. The route crosses the whole of Melbourne, and a single incident on the West Gate can hold up traffic. Avalon is a compact terminal, but you still need time for bag drop and security.

ul: Book your taxi at least a day ahead, and earlier for school holiday departures.
Allow extra time if your trip overlaps the morning peak in Melbourne.
Tell us your flight time, not just the pick-up time, so we can check your plan.
If you are travelling with a group, book one larger vehicle rather than several cars.

content.h2: Can you take wheelchairs and lots of luggage to Avalon?

For travellers without a wheelchair, a sedan suits one or two people with standard bags, and the Maxi WAT works well for families or groups with plenty of luggage. Our drivers lift bags in and out and help you to the terminal door.

content.h2: Can you collect us from Avalon when we fly home?

faq.q: Is Avalon or Melbourne Airport closer to the Mornington Peninsula?

faq.q: Can I take the Sorrento ferry to get to Avalon instead?

We can drop you at the Sorrento ferry terminal.

faq.q: Do you offer fixed quotes for Avalon trips?

For a set price, ask for a fixed quote when you book, which many groups find useful when splitting the cost.

content.h2: When should I book the taxi?

content.p: Book your bathing session first, then match your taxi times to it. Weekends and school holidays are busy at the springs, and our drivers are busy too, so book the taxi as soon as your session is confirmed.

ul: Plan to arrive a little before your session starts so check-in is not rushed.
Allow time after bathing to shower, change and dry your hair before pick-up.
Book the return trip at the same time as the drop-off.
Use “pick up when ready” if you are not sure when you will finish, and call or tap “I’m ready” when you are.

content.p: Booking online takes about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211. You will get confirmation by SMS or email.

content.h2: Can a group or a wheelchair user travel together?

content.p: Yes. Hot springs days are popular for birthdays, hens days and catch-ups with friends. A sedan suits couples, while the Maxi WAT takes six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, so a small group can arrive together and leave together. If your group is larger, we can send more than one vehicle at the same time.

For guests with mobility needs, the wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and room for one wheelchair and four companions, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist. Both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning, and carers travel with the passenger. Ask the hot springs directly about accessible bathing areas and facilities before you go, so you know what to expect on the day.

content.h2: Can you take us from a nearby resort or holiday house?

content.p: Yes. Guests staying at resorts near Fingal and Cape Schanck, or in holiday houses in Rye, Tootgarook and Blairgowrie, use us for the short trip across. It is a good way to make the hot springs part of a weekend away without moving the car. If you are visiting from Melbourne for the day, we can collect you from home, though for longer trips it is worth comparing the estimate and asking for a fixed quote.
Leaving after an evening session, you will be warm, relaxed and probably a little sleepy. Having a driver waiting means you can enjoy that feeling rather than concentrating on dark country roads.

faq.q: Is there public transport to Peninsula Hot Springs?
faq.a: Public transport to Fingal is very limited. There is no train line on the southern Peninsula, and bus services do not suit most bathing session times, especially in the evening. Many visitors without a car take a taxi from home or their accommodation and book the return trip in advance, which keeps the day simple.

faq.q: How long should I wait before booking my pick-up?
faq.a: Allow time after your bathing session ends to shower, change and collect your belongings before your taxi arrives. If you are unsure how long you will want to stay, choose “pick up when ready” and let us know when you are done by tapping “I’m ready” or calling. That way nobody is rushed out of the pools.

faq.q: Can you collect us from Peninsula Hot Springs and take us to dinner?
faq.a: Yes. Many visitors finish at the springs and head on to dinner in Sorrento, Rye, Red Hill or Mornington before going home. Tell us your plans when you book, and we can arrange the trip to the restaurant and a later pick-up to take you home, so nobody needs to drive at all.

content.p: The simplest way to do a Red Hill winery day without driving is to book a taxi from home to your first cellar door, arrange the trips between wineries, and book the ride home before you start tasting. Taxi Peninsula drives visitors to Montalto and the other cellar doors around Red Hill and Main Ridge every week. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Mornington to Montalto.

content.h2: How far is Red Hill from Mornington, and what is the drive like?

content.p: Red Hill sits in the hills in the middle of the Peninsula, inland from Dromana and Mornington. The drive from Mornington runs south through rolling farmland before climbing into the vineyards, and the roads get narrower and more winding the closer you get. Montalto is on Shoreham Road in Red Hill South, with a cellar door, a restaurant and a sculpture trail through the vines.
Those same narrow roads are the reason so many people choose a taxi. After a tasting or two and a long lunch, nobody wants to negotiate the curves in the dark or worry about blood alcohol limits.

content.h2: How much does a winery taxi day cost?

content.p: See the estimate above for the trip from Mornington to Montalto. Your whole day will depend on how many stops you add, how far you travel between them, traffic and the time of day. If you would prefer a set price for the day’s main legs, ask for a fixed quote and tell us your plan when you book.

content.h2: How do I plan a day around several cellar doors?

content.p: Start with a booking for lunch, because the restaurants fill up quickly on weekends, then plan the tastings around it. Shoreham Road has a cluster of wineries close together, so it is easy to add one or two more stops without long drives.

ul: Book your first drop-off for mid-morning so you have time for a tasting before lunch.
Book each transfer between cellar doors in advance, or use “pick up when ready” for the flexible legs.
Allow time to walk Montalto’s sculpture trail after lunch.
Book your trip home before the day starts, especially on summer weekends.
Check each cellar door’s opening days before you go, as they vary.

content.h2: Can a group or wheelchair user come too?

content.p: Yes. For couples, a sedan is all you need. For a group of friends or family, the Maxi WAT carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, so everyone travels together between stops. Larger groups can book more than one vehicle, which also gives you a little flexibility if part of the group wants to head home earlier.

Wheelchair users can travel in their chair in the accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes four seated companions, or in the Maxi WAT with its hydraulic hoist. Both vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Accessibility varies between cellar doors, so it is worth calling ahead to check paths and facilities.

content.h2: How do we get home at the end of the day?

content.p: Book your return trip when you book the drop-off. Late afternoon on a summer weekend is when every winery visitor wants a lift at once, and the hills are a long way from the nearest taxi rank. If you would rather finish when you feel like it, choose “pick up when ready”, then tap “I’m ready” or call when you are done. We will confirm when the driver is on the way.
Staying overnight on the Peninsula? We can take you from the last cellar door to your accommodation, whether that is a hotel in Mornington, a guesthouse in Red Hill or a beach house in Rye.

faq.q: Can you take us to more than one winery in a day?
faq.a: Yes. Many visitors book a sequence of trips, such as home to Montalto, Montalto to another cellar door, then home again. Let us know the order of stops when you book, or use “pick up when ready” for the flexible parts. Each leg is a separate trip on the meter unless you arrange a fixed quote.

faq.q: Do you pick up from Frankston or Melbourne for a winery day?
faq.a: Yes. We collect from Frankston, the south-eastern suburbs and anywhere in Melbourne. A longer trip to Red Hill will cost more than a local one, so check the estimate on the booking form from your address. Some visitors from Melbourne take the train to Frankston and book a taxi from there.

faq.q: Is Montalto suitable for a celebration lunch?
faq.a: Montalto has a restaurant and more casual dining areas, and it is a popular choice for birthdays and family milestones. Contact the winery directly about bookings, menus and accessibility. Once your table is booked, we can arrange taxis for the whole group so the guest of honour and everyone else can enjoy the day without driving.

content.p: Getting to the Arthurs Seat Eagle by taxi is straightforward: we drop you at the base station in Dromana or the summit station at Arthurs Seat, and pick you up at whichever station you finish at. That means you can ride the gondola one way and skip the walk or drive back. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Rosebud.

content.h2: Should I get dropped at the base or the summit?

content.p: It depends on how you want to spend the day. The Eagle runs between a base station in Dromana and a summit station at Arthurs Seat, with wide views across Port Phillip on the way. Many visitors choose the base station and ride up, so they get the views as the bay drops away behind them. Others start at the summit, explore the lookouts and nearby attractions, then ride down to the base for lunch in Dromana.

Riding one way and booking a taxi from the other station means nobody has to go back for a car. Tell us when you book which station you want to be dropped at and which one you plan to finish at, and the driver will meet you there.

Visitors from Rosebud often find the base station feels close, and it is, but the walk along the foreshore and highway with small children or older relatives is less fun than it sounds on a hot day. A short taxi ride keeps everyone fresh for the gondola and the lookouts at the top.

content.h2: How much does a taxi to the Eagle cost?

content.p: See the estimate above. The fare depends on traffic, the time of day and which station you choose, because the summit is reached by the winding Arthurs Seat Road. If you are coming from Mornington, Sorrento or Frankston, the booking form shows an estimate from your address. For a set price, ask for a fixed quote.

content.h2: When is a good time to visit?

content.p: Choose a clear day if you can, since the views across the bay are the main attraction. Weekends and school holidays are busy, so book both the gondola and the taxi ahead. Opening hours change with the season and the weather, so check with the Eagle before you set your pick-up time.

ul: Ride one way and book a pick-up at the other station.
Combine the trip with the Enchanted Adventure Garden near the summit.
Pack a warm layer, as it is often cooler and windier at the top.
Use “pick up when ready” if you are not sure how long you will stay.

content.h2: Can a family or a wheelchair user travel together?

content.p: Yes. Small families fit comfortably in a sedan, and larger groups or families with grandparents can book the Maxi WAT, which carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs. If you need child seats, mention it when you book so we can talk through what suits your children.

For passengers in a wheelchair, the accessible van with its rear ramp takes one wheelchair plus four companions, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist. Every wheelchair vehicle has four-point restraints and air-conditioning, and carers travel with the passenger. Check with the Eagle about wheelchair access to the gondola cabins before you go.

content.h2: How do we get back to Rosebud afterwards?

content.p: Book the return trip when you book the drop-off, naming the station where you will finish. Because the summit is a fair way from the nearest town, it is not somewhere you want to be waiting without a booking. If your plans are loose, use “pick up when ready” and call or tap “I’m ready” when you are done. We will confirm the pick-up spot by SMS or phone.
Many visitors finish the day with lunch or dinner in Dromana, Red Hill or McCrae. We can take you there from the station and then home to Rosebud later on, so the whole outing is car-free.

faq.q: Can you take us up Arthurs Seat Road to the summit?
faq.a: Yes. We can drop you at the summit station, which is reached by the winding road up the mountain. Some visitors prefer this so they can enjoy the summit first and ride the Eagle down. Tell us which station you want when you book, and add notes if you are meeting friends or visiting other attractions up top.

faq.q: Do you pick up from holiday parks along the foreshore?
faq.a: Yes. We collect from caravan parks and camping grounds along the Rosebud, McCrae and Dromana foreshore, as well as holiday rentals and hotels. Give us the park name and your site number, and let us know where the driver should wait, as some parks have boom gates or limited vehicle access inside.

faq.q: Can we book a pick-up at the summit and a drop at a restaurant?
faq.a: Yes. Book the trip from the summit station to your restaurant in Dromana, Red Hill or wherever you like, and then a later trip home. You can use “pick up when ready” for either leg. That way you can stay as long as you want at the top and still eat without anyone driving.

content.p: The easiest way to reach the Sorrento–Queenscliff ferry as a foot passenger is a taxi to the Searoad terminal in Sorrento, timed to the sailing you plan to catch. We drop you outside the terminal so you can walk straight in, and we can collect you again when you come back across. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Rye.

content.h2: Where is the ferry terminal, and where does the taxi stop?

content.p: Searoad Ferries runs the car and passenger ferry across the mouth of Port Phillip between Sorrento and Queenscliff, linking the Mornington Peninsula with the Bellarine. The Sorrento terminal is in the town, near the water. We drop you outside the terminal, as close to the foot-passenger entry as the set-down area allows, and tell us if you have bikes, prams or a lot of luggage so we can help unload.
From Rye, the trip runs along Point Nepean Road through Tootgarook and Blairgowrie, a lovely coastal drive that can get congested in the height of summer, when beach traffic slows everything down.

Parking near the terminal and in the Sorrento shopping strip is in heavy demand from December to February, and leaving a car for the day while you explore Queenscliff is not always easy. Arriving by taxi means you walk straight from the kerb to the ticket office, and there is no car to collect when you come back tired after a day on the Bellarine.

content.h2: How much is a taxi from Rye to the Sorrento ferry?

content.p: See the estimate above. The fare depends on traffic and the time of day, and holiday traffic through the southern towns can add a little. If you are coming from further away, such as Mornington or Frankston, the booking form shows an estimate from your address. You can ask for a fixed quote if you prefer.

content.h2: How early should I arrive for the ferry?

content.p: Check the Searoad timetable before you book, and give yourself time to buy a ticket and board without rushing. Summer weekends and school holidays bring crowds, and the drive along Point Nepean Road may be slower than you expect.

ul: Pick a sailing first, then book your taxi to arrive with a comfortable margin.
Book ahead during school holidays, long weekends and summer weekends.
If you are going on to Geelong or further, arrange your onward transport before you cross.
Bring a jacket, since the crossing can be breezy even on a warm day.

content.h2: Can you take bikes, luggage or a wheelchair?

content.p: Many people cross with bikes to ride on the Bellarine side. Tell us how many bikes you have when you book so we send a suitable vehicle. Families with prams and holiday luggage will find the Maxi WAT roomy, with space for six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs.

Passengers who travel in their chair can book the wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes four seated companions, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Four-point restraints and air-conditioning are standard. Check with Searoad about accessibility on board before your trip.

Holidaymakers staying in Rye for a week sometimes use the ferry as a day out with visiting relatives. If your group includes grandparents and small children, a single larger vehicle saves splitting up, and the driver can help everyone with bags, hats and picnic gear at the terminal.

content.h2: Can you pick us up when we come back across?

content.p: Yes. Book a return pick-up at the Sorrento terminal for the sailing you plan to catch home. Ferry times can shift with the weather and the season, so if your plans change, update the booking or call us. If you are unsure which sailing you will catch, use “pick up when ready” and let us know when you are on board or have arrived.
Some visitors make a day of it in Queenscliff and come back for dinner in Sorrento. We can collect you from the terminal and take you to a restaurant, then home to Rye later in the evening.

faq.q: Can I take the ferry and a taxi to get to Geelong?
faq.a: Yes, many people do. Cross as a foot passenger from Sorrento to Queenscliff, then continue by bus, taxi or a friend’s car on the Bellarine side. We operate on the Peninsula side, so we can take you to the Sorrento terminal and collect you on your return. Arrange your Queenscliff connection before you leave.

faq.q: Do you pick up from Portsea or Blairgowrie for the ferry?
faq.a: Yes. We collect from Portsea, Blairgowrie, Sorrento itself and anywhere along the southern Peninsula. The booking form shows a fare estimate from your exact address. For holiday houses, add any directions to the booking notes, such as a shared driveway or a gate code, so the driver can come straight to your door.

faq.q: What if the ferry is cancelled or delayed?
faq.a: Weather can affect sailings, especially in winter. If your crossing is delayed or cancelled, call us or update your booking online, and we will rearrange your pick-up. If you booked “pick up when ready” for the return, simply let us know when you are ready, and a driver will come to the terminal.

content.p: A taxi to the Stony Point ferry terminal is a direct way to connect with passenger ferries to French Island and Phillip Island without relying on the infrequent train. Taxi Peninsula drops you as close to the jetty as vehicles can go and picks you up when your ferry returns. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Frankston.

content.h2: Where is Stony Point, and which ferries leave from there?

content.p: Stony Point is on Western Port, on the eastern side of the Peninsula, at the end of the road through Hastings and Crib Point. Passenger ferries run from the terminal to Tankerton on French Island and to Cowes on Phillip Island. The terminal sits next to Stony Point railway station, but the trains on this line do not run often, so a taxi gives you more control over your timing.

From Frankston, the drive heads south-east towards Hastings and Crib Point. It is a quiet, semi-rural trip for much of the way, and we drop you near the terminal entrance, as close to the jetty as vehicles are allowed.

content.h2: How much is a taxi from Frankston to Stony Point?

content.p: See the estimate above. The fare depends on traffic, the time of day and your exact pick-up address. If you are coming from Mornington, Mount Martha or the southern Peninsula, the booking form will show an estimate from where you are. For a set price, ask for a fixed quote when you book.

content.h2: When should I book, and how do I match the ferry timetable?

content.p: Check the ferry timetable first, then book your taxi to arrive with time to spare. Ferries do not run as often as city services, and missing one can mean a long wait. Book ahead, especially on weekends and school holidays.

Weekday commuters from the islands, school groups and day-trippers all use the ferries, and sailings are spread out across the day rather than running every few minutes like city transport. If you have a fixed appointment on the other side, aim for the earlier of two possible ferries rather than the one that leaves you no margin.

ul: Choose your sailing before booking the taxi.
Allow extra time for weekday traffic through Frankston and Hastings.
Tell us about bikes, eskies or camping gear so we send the right vehicle.
Book your return pick-up before you leave for the island.
Bring a jacket, as the jetty can be windy and cold.

content.h2: Can you carry bikes, luggage and wheelchairs?

content.p: Yes. French Island has very limited roads, so many visitors travel with bikes or on foot. Let us know about bikes when you book so we send a vehicle with room. The Maxi WAT, with space for six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, suits families and groups with gear.

Wheelchair users can travel in the accessible van, which has a rear ramp for one wheelchair and four seated passengers, or in the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. The pier and gangways can vary with the tide, so check with the ferry operator about boarding access.

For island residents, the trip often runs the other way: a ferry to the mainland, then a taxi to a medical appointment, a shopping trip or a train. Our drivers will help with shopping bags and suitcases on the way back to the jetty, so you are not juggling everything on your own as the ferry boards.

content.h2: How do I get home from Stony Point?

content.p: Book a return pick-up for the ferry you plan to catch back. If you are not sure which sailing you will take, use “pick up when ready”, then call or tap “I’m ready” when you know. We will confirm the pick-up spot near the terminal by SMS or phone. Island residents crossing to the mainland for appointments can book the same way, with a taxi waiting at the jetty to take them to Frankston, the hospital or wherever they need to go.

faq.q: Do you pick up from the ferry when people arrive from the islands?
faq.a: Yes. Island residents and visitors often book us to meet the ferry at Stony Point and take them to Frankston, Mornington, a hospital appointment or a train connection. Give us the sailing time and your destination when you book, and we will confirm the pickup. If the ferry is delayed, call us and we will adjust.

faq.q: Is the train an option to get to Stony Point?
faq.a: There is a train line to Stony Point from Frankston, and the station is next to the ferry terminal. However, services on this line are not frequent, so they may not suit your ferry time. A taxi gives you door-to-door travel and lets you choose the sailing that suits you rather than fitting around the train.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi for a day trip to French Island?
faq.a: Yes. Book a drop-off for your morning sailing and a pick-up for the ferry you plan to catch back. French Island has very few roads and services, so pack water, food and sun protection. If you might return on a different sailing, use “pick up when ready” and let us know when you are on the way.

content.p: A taxi from Rosebud to Frankston Hospital is a direct, door-to-door way to reach the Peninsula’s main public hospital for appointments, tests, admissions or visiting family. Taxi Peninsula drives this route every day, in sedans and wheelchair accessible vehicles, and our drivers help you from your door to the entrance. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Rosebud.

content.h2: How long does the trip to Frankston Hospital take?

content.p: The box above gives a typical drive time. Most trips use the Mornington Peninsula Freeway and Peninsula Link before turning off towards central Frankston and the hospital on Hastings Road. Morning appointments can coincide with peak traffic around Frankston, so allow a buffer and aim to arrive a little early. Late afternoon can be slow heading back the other way.

Frankston Hospital is run by Peninsula Health and has more than one public entrance, and building works have changed access points over time. Tell us the department or ward you are visiting and we will aim for the closest step-free entrance.

Parking around the hospital is busy most of the day, so many families prefer a drop-off rather than circling for a space. It also suits visitors who want to spend a few hours with a relative on the ward without watching the clock on a parking ticket. Our driver uses the permitted set-down areas and will call you if they need to move.

content.h2: How much does the taxi cost?

content.p: See the estimate above. The final fare depends on traffic and the time of day. If you would like a set price, ask for a fixed quote when you book. We accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards, NDIS plans and aged-care accounts, so if you use one of these, mention it when booking.

content.h2: When should I book a hospital trip?

content.p: Book as soon as you have your appointment time. Morning appointments are the most popular, so booking a few days ahead gives you the most choice. If you have regular appointments, you can book a series of trips in one go.

For early procedures where you have been asked to fast or arrive before the clinic opens, book the night before at the latest, and double-check the arrival time on your letter rather than the procedure time.

ul: Book online in about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.
Add the department, clinic or ward name from your appointment letter.
Mention any mobility needs, such as a walker, wheelchair or help from the door.
Bring your Medicare card and referral letters in a bag you can keep on your lap.

content.h2: Can I travel in my wheelchair, and can someone come with me?

content.p: Yes. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs or heavier power chairs. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Carers travel with the passenger, and a family member can come along for support.
If you do not use a wheelchair but need help walking, our drivers can give you an arm from your front door to the hospital entrance, or push a hospital wheelchair if one is available at the door.

content.h2: How do I get home to Rosebud afterwards?

content.p: You can book a return trip at a set time, but appointment lengths are hard to predict. Our “pick up when ready” option suits hospital trips well. When you finish, tap “I’m ready” or call, and a driver will come to meet you. Most patients meet the taxi near the main entrance, and we will confirm the meeting point by phone or SMS.

If you are being discharged after a stay, tell us when you book so the driver knows you may need extra help with bags or getting into the car. Our discharge guide explains how this works in more detail.

faq.q: Can you take me to Rosebud Hospital instead?
faq.a: Yes. Rosebud Hospital is closer for many southern Peninsula residents and offers a range of services. We drive to both hospitals, and to private hospitals and clinics across the Peninsula and Melbourne. Check your appointment letter for the correct hospital and campus, and enter it on the booking form so the estimate is accurate.

faq.q: Can I use my MPTP card for hospital trips?
faq.a: Yes. We accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards for eligible passengers on any trip, including hospital appointments. Let us know when you book that you will be using your card. NDIS and aged-care accounts are also accepted. If you are unsure whether your trip is covered under your plan, check with your plan manager or provider.

faq.q: What if my appointment runs late?
faq.a: That is common, especially with specialist clinics, tests or day procedures. If you booked “pick up when ready”, there is nothing to change; just tap “I’m ready” or call when you are finished. If you booked a set time, call us when you know you will be late, and we will rearrange the pick-up for you.

content.p: If you are having cataract surgery at the Royal Victorian Eye and Ear Hospital, you will not be able to drive yourself home, so a door-to-door taxi from the Peninsula to Gisborne Street in East Melbourne is one of the simplest ways to get there and back. Taxi Peninsula drives patients from Mornington, Frankston and right across the Peninsula, and the trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Mornington.

facts.to: Royal Victorian Eye and Ear Hospital

content.h2: Why can’t I drive to my cataract surgery?

content.p: Cataract surgery is usually done as a day procedure, but your eye will be covered or blurry afterwards, and you may have had sedation. Your surgical team will tell you not to drive until you are cleared, which is often not the same day. Even routine eye examinations at the Eye and Ear can involve dilating drops that make driving unsafe for hours.

Cataract surgery is also often done one eye at a time, with check-ups soon after each procedure. That can add up to several trips over a few months. Many patients find it easier to book all of them with us than to ask family to take days off work for each one.

content.h2: How long does it take, and what will it cost?

content.p: The drive time and fare estimate in the box above are typical for the trip from Mornington. The route crosses the south-eastern suburbs and heads into the city, so traffic and the time of day make a difference. Morning admissions often coincide with peak hour, which can stretch the trip. The fare also depends on any tolls used. For a set price, ask for a fixed quote when you book.

content.h2: When should I book, and what should I tell you?

content.p: Book as soon as you have your admission letter. Surgery arrival times can be early, so plan your pick-up with time to spare for traffic and check-in. If you have several appointments over the coming months, you can book them together.

ul: Use the arrival time on your letter, not the procedure time, when you book.
Mention the clinic or day surgery area in the booking notes.
Let us know if you have low vision and would like to be guided to the door.
Bring sunglasses for the trip home, as bright light can be uncomfortable.
Book online in about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.

content.h2: How do I get home after the operation?

content.p: Day surgery times are hard to predict, and the hospital will release you when you are ready rather than at a fixed time. Our “pick up when ready” option suits this well. When the nurses tell you that you can go, tap “I’m ready” or call us, and a driver will come to the main entrance on Gisborne Street. We will confirm the meeting point by phone or SMS.

Your driver will guide you to the car, help you settle in and, on arrival home, walk you to your front door. If a family member or carer is coming with you, they are welcome to travel in the taxi too. Most patients prefer to rest quietly on the way home, and the driver will keep the trip calm and smooth.

content.h2: Can I travel in a wheelchair, and do you accept MPTP?

content.p: Yes. If you travel in your wheelchair, book our wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist. Both vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning.

faq.q: Can my partner come with me to the Eye and Ear?

faq.q: Do you do the trip for the follow-up appointment too?

faq.q: What if I live in Rosebud or Sorrento instead of Mornington?

content.p: For treatment at Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre, a taxi from Frankston or the Peninsula takes you from your door to the Parkville entrance and back again, without the drive into the city or the search for parking. content.h2: Where is Peter Mac, and where does the taxi drop me?

It is on Grattan Street in the Parkville health precinct, in a building it shares with other cancer services. We drop you at the main entrance set-down area, or as close as traffic and works in the precinct allow. The main entrance is step-free; tell us your clinic or treatment area when you book.
Parkville has several large hospitals close together, including The Royal Melbourne Hospital and The Royal Women’s. Name Peter Mac clearly in your booking so there is no confusion.

content.h2: How long does the trip take, and what does it cost?

Early appointments often run into peak hour. The fare depends on traffic, the time of day and tolls on the route. If you want to know the price in advance, ask for a fixed quote when you book.

content.h2: How do I manage repeat treatment trips?

content.p: Treatment often means several trips over weeks or months, sometimes several days in a row. Booking them in advance takes one task off your list. You will receive confirmation for each trip by SMS or email, so you know your ride is sorted.

ul: Book a series of trips at once if you have your treatment schedule.
Update or cancel trips online or by phone if your appointment times move.
Use “pick up when ready” for days with tests, results or uncertain finish times.
Bring a warm layer and a water bottle for long treatment days.
Book online in about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.

content.h2: Can a carer come, and can I travel in my wheelchair?

If you travel in your wheelchair, the wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs or a heavier power chair. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Our drivers help from your front door to the entrance, and on the way back to your door at home.

content.h2: How do I get home after treatment?

content.p: Treatment days can be unpredictable, and you may be tired afterwards. Our “pick up when ready” option means you do not have to guess a finish time. When you are done, tap “I’m ready” or call, and a driver will come to the front entrance. Most patients meet their driver there, and we will confirm by SMS or phone.

The trip home is a good chance to rest. If you need the temperature adjusted, a stop, or a quieter trip, just tell the driver. We accept MPTP cards for eligible passengers, as well as NDIS and aged-care accounts.

faq.q: Can I book taxis for all my treatment sessions at once?
faq.a: Yes. If you have your treatment schedule, you can book all your trips in advance, and each one is confirmed by SMS or email. If a session is rescheduled, update the booking online or call us. Many patients find this easier than arranging lifts from family for every appointment.

faq.q: Do you go to other Parkville hospitals too?
faq.a: Yes. We drive to The Royal Melbourne Hospital, The Royal Women’s Hospital and The Royal Children’s Hospital, as well as Peter Mac. These hospitals are close together in Parkville, so it is important to name the correct one when booking. Add the clinic or building name from your letter to the booking notes.

faq.q: Can a family member book the taxi on my behalf?
faq.a: Yes. Family members and carers often book on behalf of a patient. Enter the patient’s name, address and mobile number so they receive the SMS confirmation, and add notes about mobility, the clinic name and any help the driver should give. You can also book by phone if that is easier.

The campus is large, with several entrances. Tell us your clinic, department or ward when you book, and we will aim for the closest step-free entrance. Monash Children’s Hospital and the Victorian Heart Hospital are nearby but separate, so name your hospital clearly.

For Frankston families, Clayton can feel a long way for a short appointment, and the multi-storey car parks on a big campus are not much fun when you are unwell or pushing someone in a chair. Being dropped near the right door saves a long walk across the site, and it means the person driving does not miss half the appointment looking for a space.

content.h2: How long does the trip take, and how much is it?

content.p: The box above shows the usual drive time and fare estimate. The trip usually heads north through the south-eastern suburbs, and the route the driver takes depends on traffic, roadworks and the time of day. Weekday peak hours can add noticeable time. The fare depends on traffic, the time of day and any tolls. For a set price, ask for a fixed quote when you book.

If your appointment letter gives an arrival time earlier than the consultation itself, book the taxi around the arrival time. Clinics in large hospitals often ask patients to come early for paperwork, weighing or blood tests.

content.h2: When should I book?

content.p: Book as soon as you have your appointment details. Allow extra time for weekday traffic through the south-east, especially for morning appointments.

ul: Write the clinic or building name from your letter into the booking notes.
Tell us if you use a walker, wheelchair or mobility scooter.
Use “pick up when ready” for long appointments or tests.
For regular treatment, book a series of trips at once.

content.h2: Can I travel in my wheelchair, with a carer?

Choose the Maxi WAT if you use a heavy power chair or two wheelchair users are travelling, as its hydraulic hoist lifts the chair level into the vehicle and it seats six others. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Carers travel with the passenger.

If you are walking but need a little support, our drivers can help you from your front door to the hospital entrance. If you are visiting someone in hospital and have limited mobility, tell us, and the driver will help you to the door.

content.h2: How do I get home to Frankston afterwards?

content.p: Appointment lengths vary, and specialist clinics often run late. “Pick up when ready” means you can tap “I’m ready” or call when you are done, and a driver will come to you. Patients usually meet the taxi at the entrance they came in by, and we will confirm the meeting point. MPTP cards, NDIS plans and aged-care accounts are all accepted on the trip home.

faq.q: Do you also go to Dandenong or Casey Hospital?
faq.a: Yes. We drive to all Monash Health hospitals, including Dandenong Hospital and Casey Hospital, as well as Monash Children’s Hospital and the Victorian Heart Hospital. Check your appointment letter for the right hospital and campus, and enter it on the booking form so the fare estimate and drop-off point are correct.

faq.q: Can I book regular dialysis trips?
faq.a: Yes. Many patients book standing trips for regular treatment. Give us your schedule, and we will set up the trips in advance, each confirmed by SMS or email. If a session is moved, call or update online. Because dialysis can be tiring, “pick up when ready” is a good option for the trip home.

faq.q: Is a taxi easier than the train to Clayton?
faq.a: For most patients, yes. By public transport you would need to connect between trains and possibly a bus, then walk to the right building. A taxi takes you door to door, which matters when you are unwell, recovering from a procedure or using a wheelchair. You also avoid looking for parking on a busy campus.

content.p: To book a taxi home from hospital, use our “pick up when ready” option: you book the trip ahead, and when the ward releases you, you tap “I’m ready” or call, and a driver comes to meet you. Taxi Peninsula takes patients home from Frankston Hospital, Rosebud Hospital, private hospitals and Melbourne hospitals every day, in sedans and wheelchair accessible vehicles, with drivers who help from the ward entrance to your front door.

content.h2: Why is discharge hard to time?

content.p: Hospital discharge rarely happens at a predictable time. You may be told you are going home in the morning, only to wait for a doctor’s review, pharmacy medications, discharge paperwork or a final test. Family members often take time off work, only to sit in a car park for hours. Booking a taxi with a fixed time can mean a missed ride or a long, uncomfortable wait.

That is why “pick up when ready” exists. You set up the booking in advance, and we know you are coming. When the nurses tell you that you can leave, you let us know, and a driver heads to the hospital.

content.h2: How do I book a discharge taxi?

content.p: You can book online in about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211. Choose “pick up when ready” instead of a set time, and enter the hospital name and your ward. You will get confirmation by SMS or email.

ul: Enter the hospital, ward and your home address.
Choose “pick up when ready” instead of a fixed time.
Tell us about walkers, wheelchairs, crutches or anything you will be carrying.
Mention if you need help getting from the car to your front door.
When you are released, tap “I’m ready” or call us.

content.p: Family members can make the booking on your behalf. Enter your mobile number so you receive the SMS and can tap “I’m ready” yourself.

content.h2: Where will the taxi meet me?

content.p: Most patients meet the taxi near the hospital’s main entrance. Large hospitals often have several entrances, so tell us your ward when you book, and we will confirm the meeting point by phone or SMS. If you need help getting from the ward to the entrance, ask the nursing staff, as hospitals have their own arrangements for this. Once you reach the entrance, our driver takes over, helping with bags and getting you settled in the car.

content.h2: What if I need a wheelchair taxi?

content.p: If you are going home in your wheelchair, book our wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs and heavier power chairs. All wheelchair vehicles have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning.

If you normally walk but are going home on crutches or with a frame, a sedan is usually fine. Let us know so the driver can help you in and out, and fold your walking aid into the boot. Carers and family members are welcome to travel with you.

content.h2: How much does a discharge taxi cost, and can I use MPTP?

content.p: The fare depends on the hospital, your home address, traffic and the time of day. The booking form shows a fare estimate when you enter your trip, and fixed quotes are available on request. We accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards for eligible passengers, as well as NDIS and aged-care accounts. Mention which you are using when you book, so the driver is ready.
When you get home, the driver will help carry your bags and medications to the door. If your house has steps or a steep driveway, let us know in advance so the driver can plan to help.

faq.q: Can a family member book the taxi for me while I am in hospital?
faq.a: Yes. Family members and carers often book discharge taxis. Enter your name and mobile number as the passenger, so you receive the SMS and can tap “I’m ready” when the ward releases you. Add your ward and any mobility notes. If you do not have a phone with you, the nurses or your family can call us instead.

faq.q: What if I am discharged late at night?
faq.a: We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so late discharges are not a problem. Use “pick up when ready” and let us know when you are released. At night, the driver will make sure you are inside your home safely before leaving, and can help with bags and keys.

faq.q: Can you take me from hospital to a rehabilitation centre or aged-care home?
faq.a: Yes. We take patients from hospital to rehabilitation centres, aged-care homes, family homes and other destinations, not just home. Enter the destination on the booking form. If the transfer is part of an aged-care or NDIS plan, mention it when booking, and we will note the account details for the trip.

content.p: A taxi to Mornington Racecourse on race day means everyone in your group can enjoy the day, and nobody has to drive home or wait in the queue to leave the car park. On busy race days, the pick-up spot may be set by marshals. We will confirm the meeting point by SMS or phone, and the driver will call if it changes. Then it is a short, easy trip home to Mount Martha or wherever you are staying.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from a Mornington hotel for the races?

faq.q: Do you go to the racecourse for functions on non-race days?

faq.q: Can we book a taxi to go on to dinner after the races?
faq.a: Yes. Many race-goers head to dinner in Mornington or Mount Martha after the last race. Book a pick-up from the racecourse to your restaurant, then a later trip home. You can use “pick up when ready” for either part. That way the whole group can stay out without anyone needing to drive.

content.p: If your cruise ship leaves from Station Pier, a taxi from Mornington or anywhere on the Peninsula takes you and your luggage straight to the cruise terminal in Port Melbourne, with no long-stay parking to arrange. Taxi Peninsula drops you in the area set aside for cruise passengers and can collect you again when your ship returns. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from Mornington.

content.h2: How long does it take to get to Station Pier?

content.p: The box above shows a typical drive time. From Mornington the trip heads north towards the city before swinging around to Port Melbourne on the bay side. Traffic through the inner suburbs varies a lot during the day, and roads around the pier can be congested on embarkation days, especially when more than one ship is in port. Allow a comfortable buffer.

Before booking, check that your ship really departs from Station Pier. Spirit of Tasmania, for example, now sails from Geelong rather than Port Melbourne, and some cruise itineraries begin in other ports.

Driving yourself and leaving the car near the pier for a week or two can be expensive and awkward, and someone still has to drive home tired on the last morning. Friends and relatives offering a lift face the same cross-town run in both directions. A taxi turns the whole thing into one booking at each end, and the holiday starts when you shut your front door rather than when you find a parking space.

content.h2: How much is a taxi to the cruise terminal?

content.p: See the estimate above. The fare depends on traffic, the time of day and tolls on the route. If you would like the price settled before you leave, ask for a fixed quote. For groups sailing together, one larger vehicle can make the fare easier to share.

content.h2: When should I book, and what time should I arrive?

content.p: Cruise lines usually give each passenger a check-in window. Book your taxi to arrive within that window, not hours early and not at the very end of it. Embarkation days are busy, so book well ahead.

ul: Check your cruise documents for your check-in window and terminal details.
Book the taxi as soon as your sailing is confirmed.
Tell us how many suitcases you have, including garment bags.
Keep passports, documents and medications in your hand luggage, not the boot.
Book online in about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.

content.p: We drop you in the area set aside for cruise passengers. From there, follow the signs and staff instructions to check in and drop your bags.

content.h2: Can you fit all our luggage, and can a wheelchair user come?

content.p: Cruise passengers tend to pack big. A sedan suits a couple with a large suitcase each, while families or friends travelling together, or anyone with several bags, should book the Maxi WAT. It carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, so there is plenty of space for luggage when the wheelchair spaces are not in use.

Passengers who travel in their wheelchair can book the accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated companions, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Both have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Our drivers help with bags from your front door to the terminal.

content.h2: How do we get home when the ship comes back?

content.p: Passengers usually disembark early in the morning, and waiting for transport after a holiday is no fun. Book your pick-up for the morning your ship docks, and confirm the time once you are back in port. We will confirm the pick-up point by SMS or phone, and your driver will help load your bags for the trip back down to the Peninsula.
If your disembarkation group is called later than expected, call us. We will adjust the pick-up so you are not waiting in the cold or paying for a driver who has been sitting outside.

faq.q: Is Spirit of Tasmania still at Station Pier?
faq.a: No. Spirit of Tasmania now departs from Geelong, not Station Pier. If you are taking the ferry to Tasmania, check your booking and allow plenty of time for the longer drive around the bay. We can take you to Geelong as well, and the booking form will show a fare estimate for that trip.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from different addresses for a group cruise?
faq.a: Yes. If friends or family are sailing together from different Peninsula suburbs, we can collect them in turn on the way, or send separate cars that arrive together. Tell us the addresses and the number of people and bags when you book, and we will plan the most practical way to get everyone to the terminal.

faq.q: Do I need to book the return trip before I leave?
faq.a: It is a good idea. Disembarkation mornings are busy, and having a booking in place means one less thing to arrange from the ship. Book for the day your ship returns, then confirm the time once you are back in port. If anything changes, call us and we will adjust the booking.

content.p: The MPTP card is part of Victoria’s Multi Purpose Taxi Program, a government subsidy that helps eligible people with a severe and permanent disability pay for taxi and wheelchair accessible taxi trips. Card holders generally pay about half the fare, with the program covering the rest up to a cap. Taxi Peninsula accepts MPTP cards in our sedans and wheelchair accessible vehicles across the Mornington Peninsula, Frankston and Melbourne.

content.h2: What is the Multi Purpose Taxi Program?

content.p: The Multi Purpose Taxi Program is run by the Victorian Government to make taxi travel more affordable for people who cannot easily use public transport because of a severe and permanent disability. Eligibility is based on your disability and how it affects your ability to travel, rather than simply on age.

Members receive a card that they present when they take a taxi or wheelchair accessible taxi. The subsidy is applied to the fare, and the member pays the remaining part. The program is especially important on the Peninsula, where public transport is limited and many trips, such as hospital appointments in Frankston or Melbourne, are long.

content.h2: Who is eligible for an MPTP card?

content.p: Eligibility is for people with a severe and permanent disability that significantly limits their ability to use public transport. That can relate to a range of physical, sensory, intellectual or other conditions. A health professional usually needs to complete part of the application to confirm your situation.

Because eligibility rules and application processes can change, check the current details with the Victorian Government’s commercial passenger vehicle regulator before applying. Your doctor, occupational therapist or support coordinator can also help.

If you already hold a card from some years ago, it is worth checking that it is current and that your details are up to date, especially if you have moved house or your circumstances have changed. Having that sorted before a big appointment saves stress on the day.

content.h2: How does the subsidy work on a fare?

content.p: The well-known rule is that the program pays half the fare, up to a cap, and you pay the rest. If your trip is long and the fare goes over the cap, you pay the difference. The exact cap and any other limits are set by the program and can change, so check the current figures if you are planning long trips, such as to a Melbourne hospital.

ul: You present your MPTP card at the start of the trip.
The driver processes the fare with the subsidy applied.
You pay the remaining part of the fare by your usual method.
Long trips may exceed the cap, so ask for an estimate when booking.

content.p: Our booking form shows a fare estimate, and fixed quotes are available. If you are not sure how the cap will affect a particular trip, ask when you book.

For Peninsula members, the cap matters most on the long runs. A local trip from Rosebud to the shops, or from Mount Martha to a GP in Mornington, will usually sit comfortably within it. A trip to a specialist in the city, or to Melbourne Airport, may not. Knowing that in advance helps you plan, whether that means a fixed quote, combining appointments on one day, or checking whether another funding source can help with the rest.

content.h2: Can I use my MPTP card in a wheelchair taxi?

content.p: Yes. MPTP cards are accepted in wheelchair accessible taxis as well as standard taxis. Our wheelchair accessible van has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, and the Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist for two wheelchairs or heavier power chairs. All have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Carers travel with the passenger.

content.h2: How do I use my card with Taxi Peninsula?

content.p: Book online in about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211, and mention that you will be using your MPTP card. You will get confirmation by SMS or email. Have your card ready when the driver arrives. We also accept NDIS and aged-care accounts if your plan covers transport.

faq.q: Can I use my MPTP card for any trip?
faq.a: The card can generally be used for taxi trips you take as a member, such as appointments, shopping, social outings and visits. There may be limits set by the program, including a cap per trip, so check the current rules if you are unsure. Mention your card when booking with us, and we will be ready to process it.

faq.q: Can I use MPTP and NDIS together?
faq.a: Some people have both an MPTP card and NDIS funding for transport. How they work together depends on your plan and current program rules, so check with your plan manager or support coordinator. When you book with us, tell us how you intend to pay, and we will make sure the driver is prepared for the trip.

faq.q: My MPTP card is lost or damaged. Can I still travel?
faq.a: Contact the program to report a lost, stolen or damaged card and arrange a replacement. Until you have your card, the subsidy may not be able to be applied, so you may need to pay the full fare. We can still take you, and the booking form will show a fare estimate in advance.

content.p: Book a wheelchair taxi if the passenger needs to stay seated in their wheelchair during the trip, or if a power chair or scooter needs to travel with them. Book a standard taxi if the passenger can move into a car seat and their folding wheelchair or walker can go in the boot. Taxi Peninsula offers both, plus a larger Maxi WAT, so here is how to work out which one suits your trip.

content.h2: What vehicles can I choose from?

content.p: We run three types of vehicle, each suited to different needs.

ul: Sedan: a normal taxi for quick trips. It suits passengers who can get into a car seat, with folding wheelchairs, walkers or crutches in the boot.
Wheelchair accessible van: a rear ramp, room for one wheelchair plus four seated passengers.
Maxi WAT: a hydraulic hoist, room for two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers, and suited to heavier power chairs and groups.

content.p: All our wheelchair vehicles have four-point wheelchair restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Our drivers help door to door, whichever vehicle you book.

content.h2: When should I book a standard taxi?

content.p: A standard taxi is fine if the passenger can transfer safely from their wheelchair or walker into a seat, with a little help if needed. A light, folding manual wheelchair, a walking frame or a pair of crutches will usually fit in the boot. Many older passengers who use a wheelchair for longer distances, such as across a hospital, travel this way.

If you are not sure whether the transfer is safe or comfortable, especially after surgery or on a bad day, choose a wheelchair accessible vehicle. It is better to have the option and not need it than the other way around.

Think about the other end of the trip too. A passenger who can manage a transfer at home, with a familiar chair and a carer, may find it harder at a hospital entrance after a long appointment, or late at night when they are tired. If the return trip is the harder one, book the wheelchair vehicle for both legs.

content.h2: When do I need a wheelchair accessible taxi?

content.p: Book a wheelchair accessible vehicle if the passenger cannot transfer into a car seat, or needs to stay in their own chair for comfort or safety. Power chairs and mobility scooters are generally too heavy to lift into a boot, so they need a wheelchair vehicle too.

The wheelchair accessible van uses a rear ramp, which suits manual chairs and many power chairs. The Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist that lifts the chair level into the vehicle, which suits heavier power chairs and passengers who prefer not to be pushed up a ramp. If you are unsure, tell us the type of chair when you book and we will suggest the right vehicle.

Size matters as well as weight. Some tilt-in-space chairs and larger power chairs are long or tall, and a passenger with a head support may need extra headroom. Give us the make and model if you know it, or measure the chair with the passenger seated, and add those details to your booking notes.

content.h2: What about groups with more than one wheelchair?

content.p: The Maxi WAT carries two wheelchairs plus six seated passengers. It suits families where two people use wheelchairs, residents of an aged-care home going on an outing together, or a group heading to a sporting event, a winery or the airport. Carers travel with the passenger in every vehicle.

content.h2: Does a wheelchair taxi cost more, and can I use MPTP?

content.p: The booking form shows a fare estimate for your trip and vehicle, and fixed quotes are available on request. We accept Multi Purpose Taxi Program cards for eligible passengers in both standard and wheelchair taxis, as well as NDIS and aged-care accounts. Book online in about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211, and mention any mobility needs in the booking notes.

faq.q: Can I bring my mobility scooter in a taxi?
faq.a: Most mobility scooters are too heavy and bulky for a sedan boot, and many cannot be safely secured unless the passenger transfers to a seat. Tell us the make and size of your scooter when you book, and we will advise whether the wheelchair accessible van or the Maxi WAT is suitable. Ask us whether you can stay on the scooter or should move to a vehicle seat for the trip.

faq.q: Will the driver help me into the vehicle?
faq.a: Yes. Our drivers help door to door. In a sedan, they can give you an arm and fold your walker or wheelchair into the boot. In a wheelchair vehicle, they operate the ramp or hoist and secure your chair with four-point restraints. Let us know when you book if you need extra help, such as from your front door.

faq.q: Can a carer travel in the wheelchair taxi too?
faq.a: Yes. Carers travel with the passenger in all our vehicles. The wheelchair accessible van has seats for four passengers as well as one wheelchair, and the Maxi WAT seats six plus two wheelchairs. Tell us how many people are travelling when you book, so we send a vehicle with enough room for everyone.
