content.p: To book a maxi taxi for a group on the Peninsula, choose the Maxi WAT on our booking form or call us, tell us how many people are travelling and what luggage or mobility equipment you have, and book as early as you can. Our Maxi WAT carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, so a group can travel together rather than splitting across cars.

content.h2: How many people fit in a maxi taxi?

content.p: The Maxi WAT takes six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs. If no one in your group uses a wheelchair, the extra floor space is handy for luggage, eskies, golf bags or prams. For larger groups, we can send more than one vehicle at the same time, such as a Maxi WAT plus a sedan.

The Maxi WAT has a hydraulic hoist, four-point wheelchair restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. It was designed to carry wheelchair users comfortably, which also makes it roomy and easy to get in and out of for older passengers.

If your group includes young children, mention it when you book so we can talk about child seats and where everyone will sit. Babies and toddlers have specific restraint requirements, and it is far easier to sort this out on the phone a few days ahead than at the kerb.

content.h2: What do groups book a maxi taxi for?

content.p: Groups book the Maxi WAT for all sorts of trips around the Peninsula and Melbourne. Some of the most common are:

ul: Winery days in Red Hill and Main Ridge, so nobody has to drive.
Airport runs for families and friends on the same flight.
Weddings and functions, including trips from the ceremony to the reception.
Race days at Mornington and footy at the MCG.
Hot springs days, birthdays and hens or bucks outings.
Aged-care outings with residents who use wheelchairs.

content.h2: How do I book a maxi taxi?

content.p: Book online in about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211. Choose the Maxi WAT, enter your pick-up address and destination, and add notes about the size of your group, luggage and any wheelchairs. If people are coming from different addresses, list them in the notes, and we will plan the pick-ups.

Book as early as you can, especially for weekends, summer, school holidays and big events. There are only so many larger vehicles to go around on a busy Saturday, and groups often need the same times.

It helps to name one person as the group contact. They can receive the confirmation by SMS or email, keep everyone to the agreed time and talk to the driver on the day. If the group size changes, let us know early, because adding a second vehicle at the last minute on a busy evening is much harder than planning it in advance.

content.h2: How much does a maxi taxi cost for a group?

content.p: The booking form shows a fare estimate for your trip in the Maxi WAT, and fixed quotes are available on request. The fare depends on distance, traffic, the time of day and any tolls. Many groups split the fare between them, which can make a shared ride practical for longer trips, such as to the airport or a day out in the wineries.

content.h2: Can we book a maxi taxi for the trip home too?

content.p: Yes, and it is a good idea. At the end of an event or a winery day, everyone tends to want to leave at once. Book the return trip when you book the first, or use “pick up when ready” and tap “I’m ready” or call when the group is together. If some of the group want to leave early, we can send a sedan for them and the Maxi WAT for the rest.

For late nights, we operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so a group can get home safely after a wedding, a party or a concert. Our drivers help door to door, and they will wait while you gather everyone at the agreed pick-up point.

faq.q: Can the maxi taxi pick up from several addresses?
faq.a: Yes. If your group is spread across nearby suburbs, list each address in the booking notes, and we will plan the order of pick-ups. Allow extra time for each stop. If your group is spread across the Peninsula, such as Mornington and Sorrento, it may be easier to send separate vehicles that meet at the destination.

faq.q: Do you have a vehicle larger than the Maxi WAT?
faq.a: Our largest vehicle is the Maxi WAT, which carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs. For bigger groups, we can send several vehicles to travel together, such as two Maxi WATs, or a Maxi WAT and a sedan. Tell us the size of your group when you book, and we will suggest the right combination.

faq.q: Can we bring luggage, golf bags or surfboards?
faq.a: Yes, within reason. When no wheelchairs are on board, the Maxi WAT has plenty of floor space for luggage, golf bags and prams. Surfboards and other long items depend on their length. Tell us what you are bringing when you book, and we will let you know whether it fits or whether a second vehicle is needed.

title: Booking a maxi taxi for a group on the Peninsula
description: Booking a maxi taxi for a group on the Mornington Peninsula: who fits in our Maxi WAT, how to book for events, wineries and airports, and fares.
excerpt: Travelling as a group on the Mornington Peninsula? Here is how to book our Maxi WAT for winery days, airport runs, events and nights out.

content.p: For a late-night taxi home from Rye, Sorrento or Rosebud, book ahead online or by phone, ideally before you go out, and choose a set time or “pick up when ready” so you can let us know when you are leaving. Taxi Peninsula runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week, so you do not need to plan your night around the last bus. Booking ahead matters on the southern Peninsula, where taxis are not waiting on every corner.

content.h2: Why book a late-night taxi ahead of time?

content.p: The southern Peninsula is spread out, and there is no train line running to Rosebud, Rye or Sorrento. Late at night, public transport options are limited, and taxi demand spikes at closing time, after weddings, New Year’s Eve and summer weekends. A booking means your driver knows where and when to find you.

Booking ahead is especially useful if you are staying in a holiday house in Blairgowrie, Tootgarook or Capel Sound, where the streets are dark and addresses can be tricky to find. Add directions or a landmark in the booking notes.

It also takes one decision off the table at the end of the night. When nobody has a lift sorted, someone always ends up offering to drive who should not, or the group stands on the footpath trying to work out a plan. With a taxi already booked, the only question is when to leave.

content.h2: How do I book a taxi home after a night out?

content.p: Book online in about two minutes, or phone 0468 323 211. You will get confirmation by SMS or email. If you know when you will be leaving, choose a set time. If you are not sure, choose “pick up when ready”, then tap “I’m ready” or call when you want to go.

ul: Book before you go out, especially on Friday and Saturday nights.
Use “pick up when ready” if your finishing time is uncertain.
Keep your phone charged so the driver can reach you.
Agree a clear meeting point outside the venue, away from the busiest spot.
For groups, nominate one person to coordinate with the driver.

content.h2: Where should I meet the driver on Point Nepean Road?

content.p: Point Nepean Road runs through Rosebud, Rye and Sorrento and carries much of the nightlife, with pubs, restaurants and bars along it. It can be busy late on summer nights, and stopping right outside a crowded venue is not always safe. Agree a meeting point nearby, such as a side street or a car park entrance, and tell us in the booking notes. The driver will call if they need to adjust.

In winter the strip is much quieter, and venues in Rye and Sorrento may close earlier than in summer. That is when a pre-booked pick-up is most reassuring, because there are fewer people around and you do not want to be waiting on a cold, empty street.

content.h2: Can you take a group or a wheelchair user home late at night?

content.p: Yes. Small groups fit in a sedan, and larger groups can book the Maxi WAT, which carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs. If your group is going to different suburbs, we can arrange separate cars or plan the drop-offs in order.

Passengers who use a wheelchair can book the wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist. Both have four-point restraints and air-conditioning. A late night out should not depend on whether a wheelchair vehicle happens to be nearby, so book these ahead too.

content.h2: What does a late-night taxi cost?

content.p: The booking form shows a fare estimate for your trip, and fixed quotes are available on request. The fare depends on distance, traffic and the time of day, including late-night travel. MPTP cards are accepted for eligible passengers. At the end of the trip, our drivers help door to door, and they will wait until you are inside if you ask.

faq.q: Can you pick us up from a wedding venue late at night?
faq.a: Yes. We often collect guests from weddings and functions at wineries, resorts and halls across the southern Peninsula. Book before the day, give us the venue name and your finishing time, and use “pick up when ready” if the night might run late. For larger groups, book the Maxi WAT or several vehicles.

faq.q: Do you run on New Year’s Eve?
faq.a: Yes. We operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, including New Year’s Eve. It is one of the busiest nights of the year on the Peninsula, so book as early as possible, agree a clear meeting point and allow for delays. Using “pick up when ready” helps us plan when you want to leave.

faq.q: Can I book a taxi from Rye to Frankston or Melbourne late at night?
faq.a: Yes. We take passengers from the southern Peninsula to Frankston, Melbourne and anywhere in between at any hour. Longer trips take more time to plan, so book ahead if you can. The booking form shows a fare estimate, and fixed quotes are available on request if you want to know the price in advance.

content.p: A taxi from RACV Cape Schanck Resort to Melbourne Airport picks you up at the main hotel entrance on Trent Jones Drive and drops you at your terminal at Tullamarine, with your luggage and golf clubs loaded for you. Taxi Peninsula runs this transfer at any hour. The trip facts below show the distance, typical drive time and a fare estimate from the resort to the airport.

content.h2: How long does the trip from Cape Schanck take?

content.p: The box above shows a typical drive time. Cape Schanck is near the southern tip of the Peninsula, so this is one of the longer airport trips we run. The route usually heads to the Mornington Peninsula Freeway and Peninsula Link, then crosses Melbourne to the airport. Traffic through the city is the biggest variable, so allow plenty of time, particularly for weekday departures.
The roads around the resort are dark and winding at night, which is another reason many guests prefer not to drive themselves to the airport for an early flight.

Guests who drove down for a golf weekend and are flying on elsewhere, or visitors who were dropped off by friends, often find themselves at the resort without a car on departure day. Arranging the airport taxi at the start of your stay, rather than on the last evening, means one less job when you would rather be enjoying the last round or a quiet dinner.

content.h2: How much does a taxi to the airport cost?

content.p: The figure in the box above is our estimate for this trip. What you actually pay on the meter will move with the traffic, the time you travel and any tolls the driver uses on the way across Melbourne. For a long trip like this, many guests prefer a fixed quote, which we confirm by SMS or email when you book. Friends from the same golf group heading to the same flight can also share one larger vehicle.

content.h2: When should I book, and where does the taxi meet me?

content.p: Book as soon as your flight is confirmed, and at least the day before for early departures. The resort is a fair way from the nearest town, so pre-booking is the way to go rather than calling on the morning.

ul: Tell us your airline so we head to the right terminal; international flights use Terminal 2.
Add notes about golf clubs, oversized bags or a pram.
We pull up at the main hotel entrance, where reception is.
If you are attending a function or are at the golf clubhouse, tell us where to meet you.
Book online in about two minutes, or call 0468 323 211.

content.h2: Can you take golf clubs, luggage and wheelchairs?

content.p: Yes. Golfers often travel with clubs and a large suitcase each. A sedan suits a couple with standard luggage and a set of clubs, but let us know about golf bags when you book. For groups or families, the Maxi WAT carries six seated passengers plus two wheelchairs, with plenty of room for luggage when the wheelchair spaces are not in use.

Guests who use a wheelchair can book the wheelchair accessible van, which has a rear ramp and takes one wheelchair plus four seated passengers, or the Maxi WAT, which has a hydraulic hoist for heavier power chairs. Both have four-point restraints, lap-sash seatbelts and air-conditioning. Our drivers help with bags from the resort entrance to the terminal.

content.h2: Can you collect us from the airport and bring us to the resort?

content.p: Yes. Add your flight number when you book, and we will track your flight so your driver is there when you land. Airport pick-up areas are separate from the terminal doors, so we will confirm the meeting point by SMS or phone. Then it is a straight run down to the resort, so you can check in and start your stay without hiring a car.

faq.q: Can you take us to wineries or dinner during our stay?
faq.a: Yes. Guests often book us for trips to cellar doors in Red Hill and Main Ridge, dinner in Sorrento or Rye, or a visit to Peninsula Hot Springs. A taxi means nobody has to drive the dark, winding roads after a long lunch or dinner. Book ahead, especially on summer weekends.

faq.q: Do you do wedding transfers at the resort?
faq.a: Yes. Weddings at the resort often need several cars to take guests to accommodation in Rosebud, Mornington or Frankston at the end of the night. Book well before the day, give us the number of guests and their destinations, and use “pick up when ready” if the timing is uncertain.

faq.q: Is there public transport from Cape Schanck to the airport?
faq.a: Not in any practical way. Cape Schanck is a long way from the nearest train line, and the southern Peninsula has limited bus services, especially early or late in the day. Most guests arrive and leave by car or taxi. A direct taxi gives you a door-to-door trip with your luggage and clubs in one vehicle.
